prior_evidence_informing_the_expectation.source: docs/PROJECT_STATE.md 'Current metrics' table, 498k metazoa, n=1 per arm
prior_evidence_informing_the_expectation.reading: Separation ratio compares groups WITHIN a taxonomic rank, so it is largely angular rather than radial and is not the planted axis. On that already-documented evidence the canonical recipe does not merely preserve the radial prior, it produces far better angular structure. This experiment tests whether that holds at clade scale, across seeds, and on retrieval and purity as well.
prior_evidence_informing_the_expectation.caveat: Rank and depth are not identical in NCBI, so within-rank comparison controls for the planted radius substantially but not perfectly. n=1 per arm. This is why the experiment is still worth running.

preregistered_readings_step4.1_canonical_beats_prior_on_learned_metri: Figure 4's claim HOLDS, and the figure should be RE-PLOTTED on a learned metric, because the current y-axis measures the planted axis. Expected outcome given the prior evidence above.

validity_gate_per_arm: (a) training happened: max over milestones of S_angle(t) minus S_angle(init null) exceeds 10 x the within-run jitter SD (a rise-then-collapse trajectory passes this; monotonicity is NOT required)

preregistration_v2_20260922.reading_1_canonical_better: all 3 canonical seeds above all 3 prior seeds on S_angle AND canonical mean >= prior mean on S_poincare AND the canonical-minus-prior sign is positive in every depth band and every clade stratum with n >= 500 queries (clade level fixed by choose_clade_level before any embedding is read)
preregistration_v2_20260922.reading_2_equivalent: 3v3 ranges overlap AND |mean difference| < max(0.01, 2 x pooled within-arm seed SD) -- the benefit is preservation of the radial prior

preregistration_v2_20260922.attribution: Any difference is attributed to the 4-factor package (effective batch, n_negatives, lr, lr schedule), never to the batch lever alone. n_negatives interacts with the unfixed sampler's 33-100% false negatives, which are same-depth nodes -- exactly what this metric scores; re-score once Task 6 fixed-sampler runs exist.

run_1_echinodermata.verdict: INVALID -- UNINFORMATIVE. The canonical arm did not train. Do NOT read this as pre-registered reading 3.
run_1_echinodermata.executed: 2026-08-11, 6 runs (2 arms x seeds 0/1/2), 200 epochs, echinodermata_7586_clean, both arms unfixed sampler

why_invalid.canonical_trajectory_seed0: loss 5.743145 (ep1) -> 5.715695 (ep200) = -0.5%. kNN has no trend, wandering 48.9-74.5%. Separation flat 0.88-0.89, IDENTICAL to its value after 2 epochs. This is noise, not learning.
why_invalid.mechanism: epoch_fraction 0.3 over 34,938 pairs is ~10,481 pairs/epoch. Canonical (batch 256, grad-accum 8) gets ~5.1 optimizer steps/epoch at lr 0.001 with cosine decay; prior (batch 128, grad-accum 4) gets ~20.5 at lr 0.005 constant. Four times fewer steps at a fifth the LR. The recipe is scale-aware BY DESIGN and echinodermata is ~125x smaller than the metazoa scale where Figure 4's contrast was measured.
why_invalid.also_not_cross_comparable: n_negatives 300 vs 100 changes the softmax denominator, so the arms' absolute losses differ by construction. Only within-arm trajectories are meaningful here.

run_1_echinodermata.defect_in_this_preregistration: The three pre-registered readings covered outcomes but included NO VALIDITY GATE, so a run in which one arm never trains maps onto 'prior beats canonical' by default. Any re-run must gate on both arms showing a real loss decrease and a trending learned metric before the contrast is read at all.
run_1_echinodermata.what_it_does_establish: Nothing about the recipe claim. It does independently re-confirm that depth-norm r is planted: both arms sit at +0.980 to +0.982 from epoch 1 onward, including the arm that learned nothing at all. An arm with a flat loss and directionless kNN still scores +0.980 on the metric Figure 4 uses as its y-axis. That is the Task 4 finding reproduced from the opposite direction.

run_2_mollusca_200ep.verdict: TRAINING GATE PASSED, CONVERGENCE GATE FAILED for canonical. Still not decisive, but far more informative than run 1.
run_2_mollusca_200ep.executed: 2026-08-11, 6 runs (2 arms x seeds 0/1/2), 200 epochs, mollusca_6447_clean (32,017 nodes, 278,695 pairs), both arms unfixed sampler

training_gate.canonical_seed0: loss 5.712142 -> 5.303981 (-7.1%), which is ~99x its own last-10-epoch noise span of 0.004129. kNN climbs 32.7% (ep125) -> 63.5 (150) -> 85.1 (175). PASSES: this arm trained, unlike at echinodermata.

convergence_gate.detail: Prior flattens by ~ep100-125 (loss pinned at 3.81, kNN at ~99%). Canonical is still improving at ep200 (loss 5.394 ep150 -> 5.318 ep175 -> 5.304 ep200; kNN still climbing). Comparing a converged arm against a still-improving one at a fixed epoch budget is not a fair contrast.
convergence_gate.structural_cause: Canonical takes 4x fewer optimizer steps per epoch BY CONSTRUCTION (batch 256/accum 8 vs 128/accum 4). At equal epochs it gets a quarter of the steps. At metazoa/cellular scale both arms get hundreds of thousands of steps and this is moot; at 32k nodes it decides the outcome.
convergence_gate.fix: Match optimizer STEPS, not epochs. Canonical at 800 epochs is ~32,640 steps, matching prior's 200 epochs at ~32,660.

pattern_emerging_NOT_a_verdict.observation: Canonical holds depth-norm at +0.990 flat from epoch 1 and it never moves. Prior's depth-norm DIPS to 0.896 by epoch 2, recovers to 0.987 by ep75, and settles at 0.972 -- while its kNN reaches 99.6% and separation 1.13 against canonical's 73.4% and 1.02.
pattern_emerging_NOT_a_verdict.reading: This is pre-registered reading 2's signature: the canonical recipe's demonstrated benefit looks like PRESERVATION OF THE RADIAL PRIOR rather than acquisition of angular structure. NOT CALLED, because a non-converged arm cannot be compared against a converged one.
pattern_emerging_NOT_a_verdict.guard: Do not let this pattern harden into a conclusion before the step-matched run and the arthropoda run report. It is currently confounded with step count.
